nodes.label: Function-call keys bind receiver, optional method names and gas allowance, prohibit attached NEAR, and remain distinct from full-access keys.
Meta transactions bind sender, receiver, action list, public key, nonce and maximum block height before signing.
DefusePayload binds signer_id, verifying_contract, deadline, nonce and flattened intent content; the source contains a TODO to add version and calls SignedPayload an internal unstable API.
MultiPayload uses a standard tag for seven supported wallet signature formats and extracts a shared DefusePayload.
NEP-413 extraction takes signer and deadline from message JSON, verifying contract from envelope recipient, and nonce from envelope nonce.
ERC-191 carries a payload string and recoverable signature; public key is recovered, and DefusePayload is parsed directly from the string.
NEP-413 hashes Borsh encoding of the offchain prefix tag and message/32-byte nonce/recipient/optional callback URL using SHA-256; tag is 2147484061.
ERC-191 prehash is Keccak256 of Ethereum signed-message prefix, decimal byte length, and exact message bytes.
The engine verifies signature, extracts payload, checks verifying contract/deadline/key membership, validates and commits nonce, executes intents and finalizes accounting.
TokenDiff encodes exact signed i128 deltas as strings, applies them to signer balances, computes fees on negative deltas and credits the fee collector.
TransferMatcher finalization rejects nonempty unmatched per-token deltas and overflow.

sign validates domain/protocol and payload, binds predecessor and derivation path, queues a yield; respond checks an attested signer and cryptographic response; private callback distinguishes signature from timeout.
Current sign args serialize path,payload_v2,domain_id; legacy payload/key_version aliases are accepted separately, and conflicting old/new fields reject. Derived tweak uses predecessor_id and path.
Payload distinguishes hex-encoded Ecdsa fixed-length bytes from bounded Eddsa message bytes.
SDK example composes asynchronous calls with and/then and passes explicit Result<T,PromiseError> to private callbacks, distinct from callback_unwrap.
The checked-out Rust SDK quote schema distinguishes exact input/output, assets, slippage, deposit/refund/recipient types, deadline and app fees; it lists only ORIGIN_CHAIN and INTENTS deposit types.
Overview describes broad desired outcomes and solver quote approval followed by verifier settlement; it does not specify a universal proof relation.

Current 1Click docs distinguish origin-chain deposits from INTENTS/CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS wallet-signed execution using generate-intent and submit-intent; partner authentication is separate from user signedData.
1Click quote signature authenticates origin and field integrity using a Base58 SHA-256 hash of stable-key JSON combining quote request, response and timestamp.
Current signing docs specify key/signature sizes, uncompressed ECDSA coordinates, raw concatenated signatures, NEP-413 base64 nonce, and ERC-191 recovery-byte normalization.
1Click docs describe quote collection, construction, status, retries and refunds behind a REST API; its no-custody statement is documentation, not an independently verified property here.
Current docs distinguish unauthenticated quotes and authenticated partner fee schedules; partner JWT is sent in X-API-Key or Authorization Bearer.
Docs explicitly permit any quoting mechanism and direct chain indexing without Message Bus; bus bundles matching signed intents for verifier settlement.
Hosted solver-relay-v2 RPC requires partner JWT; quote takes asset identities, exactly one input/output amount and minimum deadline.
Current docs describe compliance screening on integrated quote flows, with coverage varying by flow and integration path.
execute_intents is pausable and panics on engine/final accounting errors; simulation uses a cached state. Neither entrypoint is a universal proof checker.
Contract State adapters detach withdrawals, notifications and auth calls; successful engine execution is not evidence that those asynchronous effects have settled.
NEP141 deposit execution selects inline execute_intents when refund_if_fails is true and a detached self-call otherwise. The choice changes the receipt boundary and recovery behavior.

FT resolver treats failed ft_transfer as zero used but failed ft_transfer_call as fully used to avoid unsafe refund after possible downstream effects; malformed successful transfer-call JSON is a separate zero-used branch.
Intents key membership supports an implicit account/key identity for an absent stored account; explicit prior key registration is not universally necessary.
MPC duplicate request keys can have multiple queued yields. get_pending_request returns an arbitrary representative for presence only; timeout removes one FIFO slot, leaving siblings pending.

SDK builder binds verifying contract, signer, ISO deadline, versioned nonce and intents. Its atomicity comment must be scoped to synchronous acceptance because contract state adapters schedule detached external work.
SDK getQuote rejects replies with wrong asset identities or wrong fixed input/output amount and uses BigInt to rank admissible candidates; this is proposal checking rather than settlement proof.
1Click detailed quote API defines deadline as the timestamp when refund begins if the swap is incomplete, unlike quickstart wording calling it quote expiration. Dry quotes omit execution fields.

Current generate-intent docs describe target-state and conditional caller-ownership checks; swap_transfer takes depositAddress, signerId and standard. They do not specify a duplicate-request idempotency guarantee.

Current submit-intent docs return intentHash and correlationId upon successful submission; the sampled API does not specify duplicate submission semantics or establish destination settlement at that response.
Current quote API supports FLEX_INPUT partial deposits with lower bounds and ANY_INPUT restricted to authorized partners; route availability is service policy.

Message Bus publish_intents prose promises retries but its requote field defaults false and describes retry when true. Treat automatic retry as conditional and preserve this documentation inconsistency.
1Click origin deposit notification is optional; tracking uses deposit address. SUCCESS means delivered according to the service documentation; FAILED is distinct from REFUNDED.
